This indicates that Sinocalycanchinensin G may modulate TNFRSF5 through a signaling cascade involving kinases and their downstream effectors. The presence of a shared target, [(2R,3S,4R,5R,6R)-6-[...]-yl]methyl acetate, further supports the notion that Sinocalycanchinensin G interacts with TNFRSF5 via a common intermediate. The mechanism appears to involve the activation of signaling pathways that ultimately lead to the regulation of TNFRSF5, though the exact molecular details remain to be fully elucidated. The evidence is consistent with a role in the TNFRSF5 signaling network, but further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct interaction and the precise mechanism of action.
